replies.author: @AFSoldiergal
replies.text: Your mortgage payment has two parts: the Note (principal and interest) and the Escrow Account (homeowners insurance and property taxes). The Note stays the same, while escrow usually increases over time, so it's important to understand how it works.. I pay extra toward both my principal (the Note) and escrow account each month because I know escrow will likely increase. In 19 years, it only decreased once...by about $20. Since I overfund my escrow, my annual payment increase is usually only $5–$10 (or less), and I receive an escrow refund check that I simply put back into the escrow account.  Also, research strategies for paying off your mortgage early.
